thread:
nina: thinking out loud — can we expand spot pools to include 4-5 GPU families (A100/H100/A10G/L4/T4) with multi-instance-type fleets? goal: cut cost per-token by ~20% without breaking tail latency SLOs. tradeoffs?

sam: i'm +1 on diversification from a cost POV. main worry is the variance in throughput and memory across types — packing models that assume 80GB KV cache onto 40GB cards will get messy. :thinking_face:

leo: agree with sam. also the preemptible signal timing differs by cloud/provider. we need a single interruption-handling surface: checkpointing + fast reschedule. otherwise tasks will flail.

anya: quick notes from experiments last quarter: mixed fleets saved ~18% on avg but 95p latency increased ~7-10% for long-context models. root cause was bin-packing that forced cross-type placement and frequent model reloads.

nina: that matches my expectation. two ideas: (1) smart bin-packing that is GPU-aware (memory, PCIe/NVLink, compute), (2) instance-class preference policy — prefer cheaper instance for short jobs and stable classes for long-running sessions.

leo: what does GPU-aware bin-packing look like? more than just memory and vram. e.g., NVLink topology matters for model parallelism, MIG slices change perf characteristics. we should include perf-profile vectors per model: {throughput_tokens_s, kv_memory_bytes, cold-start_seconds}.

sam: +1 to model perf vectors. we currently store a rough perf matrix in redis. maybe extend it to include cost_per_token estimate for each (model, instance_type) pair. then pack by cost with constraints.

marta: can we see an example config? something like k8s nodeAffinity + multiple provisioning groups?

nina: example ASG/spotfleet-ish policy (pseudo):

```
spot_pool:
  name: mixed-gpu-pool-1
  preferred_types: [h100, a100, a10g]
  fallback: [l4, t4]
  packing_strategy: cost-aware-best-fit
  preempt_policy:
    checkpoint: incremental
    signal_handler: 120s
    fast_fallback_to_reserved: true
```

leo: + code snippet makes sense. major implementation items: 1) cost-aware-best-fit algorithm (multi-dim knapsack), 2) graceful model migration instrumentation (KV cache dump/load), 3) scheduling knobs for session length.

anya: regarding interruptions — we saw ~12% of spot evictions where our signal handler didn't finish checkpointing due to noisy neighbor grace windows. we should track "signal_to_checkpoint_complete_ms" metric and abort if > threshold, then fallback to on-demand node migration.

sam: ops concerns — more instance types increases image/driver permutations. we need golden AMIs/VM images per family and automated smoke tests: cudnn + triton + nvidia-driver matrix. otherwise we get opaque failures in prod.

marta: also need pricing telemetry: spot_price_history + interruption_rate_by_type + effective_cost_per_token_by_type. finance will want daily rollups.

nina: suggestion for rollout: start with A100 + A10G pair in one pool (same architecture family if possible), run 4-week canary on non-prod traffic. measure: cost_delta, 95p_latency_delta, reschedule_success_rate, avg_checkpoint_time. if stable, expand to H100 and cheaper L4 for small/short jobs.

leo: one more operational idea — separate pools by session length class (ephemeral <5min, short 5-30min, long >30min). ephemeral can be aggressive spot-first; long sessions prefer reserved or H100-only. simpler to pack and predict.

sam: let's also add autoscaler TTLs tuned by instance_family — avoid scale-down thrashing when mixed instances have different ramp times.

anya: will create a short RFC doc with perf-matrix schema and metrics after standup. can we add `devops-bot` to auto-post the daily interruption table?

devops-bot: scheduled: will post "spot-interruptions/daily" report at 06:00 UTC starting tomorrow. includes interruption_rate_by_type and median_signal_lead_time_ms. :white_check_mark:

marta: sounds good. finance: if we can consistently show >=15% net cost reduction with <5% 95p latency regression, they greenlight expanded spot usage.

nina: awesome — thanks everyone. next steps: anya to draft RFC, leo to prototype cost-aware bin-packer, sam to scope AMI matrix and smoke tests, marta to wire finance metrics. i'll coordinate canary start in two weeks. :rocket:
